steps.note: Fetch. Read the two bytes at address 00 (10 00) into the instruction register. The program counter moves on to 02.
Decode. Split 10 = 0001 00 00: opcode 1 is LDI, rd = R0, rs = R0. So this is LDI R0, 00.
Execute. R0 = 00, the value carried in the instruction itself.
Fetch. Read the two bytes at address 02 (24 80) into the instruction register. The program counter moves on to 04.
Decode. Split 24 = 0010 01 00: opcode 2 is LD, rd = R1, rs = R0. So this is LD R1, [80].
Execute. R1 = mem[80] = 03.
Fetch. Read the two bytes at address 04 (18 01) into the instruction register. The program counter moves on to 06.
Decode. Split 18 = 0001 10 00: opcode 1 is LDI, rd = R2, rs = R0. So this is LDI R2, 01.
Execute. R2 = 01, the value carried in the instruction itself.
Fetch. Read the two bytes at address 06 (74 0E) into the instruction register. The program counter moves on to 08.
Decode. Split 74 = 0111 01 00: opcode 7 is JZ, rd = R1, rs = R0. So this is JZ R1, 0E.
Execute. R1 is 03, not zero, so no jump: pc stays 08.
Fetch. Read the two bytes at address 08 (41 00) into the instruction register. The program counter moves on to 0A.
Decode. Split 41 = 0100 00 01: opcode 4 is ADD, rd = R0, rs = R1. So this is ADD R0, R1.
Execute. R0 = R0 + R1 = 00 + 03 = 03 (the ALU's adder).
Fetch. Read the two bytes at address 0A (56 00) into the instruction register. The program counter moves on to 0C.
Decode. Split 56 = 0101 01 10: opcode 5 is SUB, rd = R1, rs = R2. So this is SUB R1, R2.
Fetch. Read the two bytes at address 0C (60 06) into the instruction register. The program counter moves on to 0E.
Decode. Split 60 = 0110 00 00: opcode 6 is JMP, rd = R0, rs = R0. So this is JMP 06.
Execute. Jump: pc = 06. This is how a loop goes back to its top.
Fetch. Read the two bytes at address 06 (74 0E) into the instruction register. The program counter moves on to 08.
Decode. Split 74 = 0111 01 00: opcode 7 is JZ, rd = R1, rs = R0. So this is JZ R1, 0E.
Execute. R1 is 02, not zero, so no jump: pc stays 08.
Fetch. Read the two bytes at address 08 (41 00) into the instruction register. The program counter moves on to 0A.
Decode. Split 41 = 0100 00 01: opcode 4 is ADD, rd = R0, rs = R1. So this is ADD R0, R1.
Execute. R0 = R0 + R1 = 03 + 02 = 05 (the ALU's adder).

Execute. Jump: pc = 06. This is how a loop goes back to its top.

Execute. R1 is 01, not zero, so no jump: pc stays 08.

Decode. Split 41 = 0100 00 01: opcode 4 is ADD, rd = R0, rs = R1. So this is ADD R0, R1.
Execute. R0 = R0 + R1 = 05 + 01 = 06 (the ALU's adder).

Decode. Split 56 = 0101 01 10: opcode 5 is SUB, rd = R1, rs = R2. So this is SUB R1, R2.

Decode. Split 60 = 0110 00 00: opcode 6 is JMP, rd = R0, rs = R0. So this is JMP 06.
Execute. Jump: pc = 06. This is how a loop goes back to its top.

Execute. R1 is zero, so jump: pc = 0E. The loop is over.
Fetch. Read the two bytes at address 0E (30 81) into the instruction register. The program counter moves on to 10.
Decode. Split 30 = 0011 00 00: opcode 3 is ST, rd = R0, rs = R0. So this is ST R0, [81].
Execute. mem[81] = R0 = 06.
Fetch. Read the two bytes at address 10 (00 00) into the instruction register. The program counter moves on to 12.
Decode. Split 00 = 0000 00 00: opcode 0 is HLT, rd = R0, rs = R0. So this is HLT.
Execute. HLT: the CPU stops. The answer 6 is in memory at 81.
